item.title: devvm
item.description:
Open a shell in this folder’s VM, creating it first

Synopsis

Open a shell in this folder’s VM, at the same path, and create the VM first when the folder has none. devvm shows what a new VM gets, and in a terminal you can customize its toolchains, coding agents, layers, tier, ports and size, which –tools, –agents, –layers, –network, –ports, –cpus, –memory and –disk choose without asking. The VM mounts only this folder read-write, and with –clone it gets its own clone of the repo instead.

devvm [flags]

Examples 

 devvm # open this folder's VM, choosing what a new one gets
 devvm --agents claude # create the VM with Claude Code and the toolchains the folder needs
 devvm --tools node --agents none --layers docker # create the VM with node and the docker layer alone
 devvm --clone # create the VM with its own clone of this repo
 devvm ls # list every VM

Options 

 --agents LIST the LIST of coding agents a new VM gets, such as claude,codex, or none (default: devvm setup's)
 --clone create the VM with its own clone of this repo, or of each repo in this folder, instead of mounting the folder
 --cpus N the N CPUs the VM gets (default: devvm size -g, else the image's)
 --disk GiB the VM's disk in GiB, at least the image's (default: devvm size -g, else the image's)
 --from IMAGE the container IMAGE base starts from, such as node:24, instead of Ubuntu's cloud image (default: $DEVVM_FROM)
 -h, --help help for devvm
 --here use this folder's own VM, never that of a folder it's inside
 --layers LIST the LIST of layers a new VM's image gets, bottom first, such as docker,mine, or none (default: devvm setup's)
 --memory GiB the VM's memory in GiB, such as 16 or 16G (default: devvm size -g, else the image's)
 --network TIER the network TIER a new VM gets: open, internet, allowlist or none, or learn for internet while it learns the hosts it needs (default: devvm network -g's, else allowlist)
 --no-devcontainer create the VM without reading the folder's devcontainer.json
 --no-git-protect create the VM without .git protection
 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 --parent use the VM of the nearest folder this one is inside, even across a git repo of its own
 --ports PORTS the PORTS the VM forwards: all, none or a list like 5173,8000-8010 (default: devvm ports -g, else all)
 --repos LIST the repos a --clone VM of a folder of repos gets: all, none or a LIST of their paths, such as frontend,backend (default: a picker in a terminal)
 --ssh-agent create the VM with your SSH agent forwarded, so anything in it can use your keys while you're connected
 --ssh-config add devvm's Include line to ~/.ssh/config without asking
 --tools LIST the LIST of toolchains a new VM gets, such as node,python, or none (default: those the folder's files call for)
 --unsafe-folder mount a folder devvm refuses, such as your home folder
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line
 --version print devvm's version

Docs

The docs page for devvm explains it in full.

item.title: devvm adopt
item.description:
Give this folder the VM made for an earlier folder or path

Synopsis

Give this folder the VM made for an earlier folder at this path, or for this folder before you moved or renamed it, with its files, secrets and allowlist. With VM, its name as devvm ls lists it, devvm moves that VM here from a folder that’s gone, such as one you copied to another disk. devvm asks first in a terminal without –no-input.

devvm adopt [VM] [flags]

Examples 

 devvm adopt # give this folder the VM, after asking
 devvm adopt --force # give it without asking, as a script must
 devvm adopt devvm-web-71a99b1076d92c # move that VM here from a folder that's gone, after asking

Options 

 -f, --force don't ask to confirm, which devvm needs without a terminal or with --no-input
 -h, --help help for adopt

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line

Docs

The docs page for devvm adopt explains it in full.

See also

  • devvm: Open a shell in this folder’s VM, creating it first

item.title: devvm agent
item.description:
Fill devvm’s store of the agents’ settings and logins that every VM gets

Synopsis

devvm keeps the coding agents’ settings in ~/.config/devvm/agents and their logins in ~/.local/share/devvm/logins, and every VM with an agent gets them from there, never from the agents’ own files in your home folder. devvm agent login saves a login made in this folder’s VM, devvm agent import copies those files into the store once, and devvm agent save copies a VM’s settings into it.

devvm agent [flags]

Examples 

 devvm agent login codex # log Codex in, in this folder's VM, for every VM
 devvm agent import # copy every agent's settings and logins from this machine
 devvm agent import codex # copy only Codex's
 devvm agent save # copy the settings of this folder's VM's agents, after showing what changed

Options 

 -h, --help help for agent

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line

Docs

The docs page for devvm agent explains it in full.

See also

  • devvm: Open a shell in this folder’s VM, creating it first
  • devvm agent import: Copy the agents’ settings and logins from this machine into devvm’s store
  • devvm agent login: Log an agent in, in this folder’s VM, and save the login in devvm’s store
  • devvm agent save: Copy the agents’ settings from this folder’s VM into devvm’s store

item.title: devvm agent import
item.description:
Copy the agents’ settings and logins from this machine into devvm’s store

Synopsis

Copy the settings and logins of AGENT, claude, codex, opencode, pi or cursor, or of every agent, from your home folder into devvm’s store, never their history. It copies what a link out of an agent’s folder leads to only from a folder that config.toml’s follow-links names, or after naming the link and asking, which –follow-links answers. It asks before replacing what the store has.

devvm agent import [AGENT...] [flags]

Examples 

 devvm agent import # copy every agent's settings and logins, asking before replacing the store's
 devvm agent import claude codex # copy only Claude Code's and Codex's
 devvm agent import --force # replace the store's without asking, as a script must
 devvm agent import --follow-links # copy what links out of the agents' folders lead to as well, such as into a dotfiles repo

Options 

 --follow-links copy what links out of the agents' folders lead to, naming each, without asking (default: ask in a terminal)
 -f, --force don't ask to confirm, which devvm needs without a terminal or with --no-input
 -h, --help help for import

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line

Docs

The docs page for devvm agent import explains it in full.

See also

  • devvm agent: Fill devvm’s store of the agents’ settings and logins that every VM gets

item.title: devvm agent login
item.description:
Log an agent in, in this folder’s VM, and save the login in devvm’s store

Synopsis

Log AGENT in inside this folder’s VM, and keep the login in devvm’s store for every VM with the agent, which gets only placeholders. claude logs in through a browser on any machine, whose code you paste back, or gets a long-lived Claude Code token with –setup-token. codex and opencode log in to ChatGPT in a browser on this machine, or with a code with –device-code, or save an API key with –api-key, which is pi’s only login.

devvm agent login AGENT [flags]

Examples 

 devvm agent login claude # log Claude Code in to your Claude subscription
 devvm agent login claude --setup-token # get a Claude Code token with claude setup-token instead
 devvm agent login codex # log Codex in to ChatGPT in a browser on this machine
 devvm agent login codex --device-code # log in with a code, in a browser on any machine
 devvm agent login opencode --api-key --provider anthropic # save opencode's Anthropic API key, asking for it
 devvm agent login pi --api-key --provider openai # save pi's OpenAI API key, asking for it

Options 

 --api-key save an API key instead, asking for it
 --device-code log in with a code to type into a browser on any machine, so nothing is forwarded
 -h, --help help for login
 --here use this folder's own VM, never that of a folder it's inside
 --parent use the VM of the nearest folder this one is inside, even across a git repo of its own
 --provider PROVIDER with opencode's or pi's --api-key, the PROVIDER it's for: anthropic, deepseek, google, groq, mistral, openai, openrouter or xai
 --setup-token with claude, get a long-lived Claude Code token with claude setup-token instead
 --stdin read the secret from a line of input, without asking

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line

Docs

The docs page for devvm agent login explains it in full.

See also

  • devvm agent: Fill devvm’s store of the agents’ settings and logins that every VM gets

item.title: devvm agent save
item.description:

item.title: devvm build
item.description:
Build an image and the images under it, unless they’re built

Synopsis

Build an image and the images under it, unless they’re built. IMAGE is base, or layers joined with + bottom first, so foo+bar is bar on foo on base. An image holds no shared tools: a VM gets those when devvm makes it, or with devvm tools.

devvm build IMAGE [flags]

Examples 

 devvm build docker # build base and the docker layer on it
 devvm build foo+bar # build base, foo and foo+bar

Options 

 --from IMAGE the container IMAGE base starts from, such as node:24, instead of Ubuntu's cloud image (default: $DEVVM_FROM)
 -h, --help help for build

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it

item.title: devvm clone
item.description:
Show or change whether this folder’s VM has its own clone of the repo

Synopsis

Show whether this folder’s VM has its own clone of the repo, or of each repo in a folder of repos, on, or mounts this folder, off. devvm clone on and devvm clone off make the VM again from its image, after asking in a terminal without –no-input, then open a shell in it, and devvm keeps its home folder and its settings, while everything else on its disk is lost. On copies the repos’ branches into the new clone, and off first offers to fetch the clone’s work into this machine’s repos, unless you give –no-clone-check.

devvm clone [on|off] [flags]

Examples 

 devvm clone # show whether the VM has its own clone of the repo
 devvm clone on # make the VM again with its own clone of the repo, after asking
 devvm clone off # fetch the clone's work, then make the VM again with this folder mounted
 devvm clone on --force # make it again without asking, as a script must
 devvm clone fetch # fetch the VM's branches into each repo on this machine

Options 

 --clean-home give the VM the image's home folder instead of keeping its own
 -f, --force don't ask to confirm, which devvm needs without a terminal or with --no-input
 -h, --help help for clone
 --here use this folder's own VM, never that of a folder it's inside
 --json print it as one JSON object, for scripts
 --no-clone-check don't check a --clone VM's clone for unfetched commits and uncommitted changes first, which are lost
 --no-export don't export the agents' history first
 --parent use the VM of the nearest folder this one is inside, even across a git repo of its own
 --repos LIST the repos a --clone VM of a folder of repos gets: all, none or a LIST of their paths, such as frontend,backend (default: a picker in a terminal)

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line

Docs

The docs page for devvm clone explains it in full.

See also

  • devvm: Open a shell in this folder’s VM, creating it first
  • devvm clone add: Copy one more repo into this folder’s –clone VM
  • devvm clone fetch: Fetch the work of this folder’s –clone VM into each of its repos

item.title: devvm clone add
item.description:
Copy one more repo into this folder’s –clone VM

Synopsis

Copy the repo at PATH, a folder in this folder’s –clone VM’s folder, into the VM at the same path, with its branches, tags and remote-tracking branches, checked out as it is here, starting the VM if it’s stopped. The repo gets a remote for the VM, as each of the VM’s repos has.

devvm clone add PATH [flags]

Examples 

 devvm clone add tools # copy the repo in ./tools into the VM
 devvm clone add ../shared # copy a repo beside this one, in the same folder of repos

Options 

 -h, --help help for add
 --here use this folder's own VM, never that of a folder it's inside
 --parent use the VM of the nearest folder this one is inside, even across a git repo of its own

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line

Docs

The docs page for devvm clone add explains it in full.

See also

  • devvm clone: Show or change whether this folder’s VM has its own clone of the repo

item.title: devvm clone fetch
item.description:
Fetch the work of this folder’s –clone VM into each of its repos

Synopsis

Fetch every branch of each repo in this folder’s –clone VM into the repo on this machine, as remote-tracking branches of its remote for the VM, such as devvm/main, starting the VM if it’s stopped. When a repo’s HEAD in the VM is detached at commits no branch has, fetch those into a new local branch, saved/devvm/HEAD, and each stash entry the VM made into saved/devvm/stash-N. Then list the branches that are new or moved, each with the repos it’s in.

devvm clone fetch [flags]

Examples 

 devvm clone fetch # fetch every repo's branches, and list what's new
 devvm clone fetch --json # list what's new for a script

Options 

 -h, --help help for fetch
 --here use this folder's own VM, never that of a folder it's inside
 --json print it as one JSON object, for scripts
 --parent use the VM of the nearest folder this one is inside, even across a git repo of its own

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line

Docs

The docs page for devvm clone fetch explains it in full.

See also

item.title: devvm completion
item.description:
Print the shell completion script for bash, zsh or fish

Synopsis

Print the script that completes devvm’s commands, flags, image names and shared tools in SHELL, which is bash, zsh or fish. Load it from your shell’s startup file.

devvm completion SHELL [flags]

Examples 

 source <(devvm completion bash) # in ~/.bashrc, with the bash-completion package installed
 source <(devvm completion zsh) # in ~/.zshrc, after compinit
 devvm completion fish | source # in ~/.config/fish/config.fish

Options 

 -h, --help help for completion

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it

item.title: devvm desktop
item.description:
Open this folder’s VM’s desktop in a VNC viewer

Synopsis

Start the desktop of this folder’s VM, which needs the desktop layer, and serve it on this machine’s 127.0.0.1 with a password of the VM’s own until you press Ctrl+C or the VM stops. On macOS, Screen Sharing opens it and asks for the password, which devvm shows.

devvm desktop [flags]

Examples 

 devvm desktop # open the VM's desktop in Screen Sharing
 devvm desktop --clipboard # the same, sharing the clipboard both ways
 devvm desktop --no-open # show the address and password for a VNC viewer of your own

Options 

 --clipboard share the clipboard between this machine and the VM, both ways
 -h, --help help for desktop
 --here use this folder's own VM, never that of a folder it's inside
 --no-open show the address and password without opening Screen Sharing
 --parent use the VM of the nearest folder this one is inside, even across a git repo of its own

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line

Docs

devvm doctor [flags]

Examples 

 devvm doctor # check what devvm needs
 devvm doctor --json # the same as JSON, for scripts

Options 

 -h, --help help for doctor
 --json print what it found as JSON, and succeed whatever is missing

Options inherited from parent commands

item.title: devvm gc
item.description:
Delete stale images, unused tools, old files and the Nix cache over its cap

Synopsis

Delete the stale and unfinished images, the shared tools devvm images lists as unused, the files devvm itself no longer needs, and the shared Nix cache’s least recently used files while it’s over its cap, after listing them and asking in a terminal without –no-input. Its flags delete more, such as –tool-images for the current shared tool images no VM has. gc never deletes a VM.

devvm gc [--tool-images [TOOL...]] [flags]

Examples 

 devvm gc # delete stale images and unused tools, after asking
 devvm gc --tool-images # also the current shared tool images no VM has
 devvm gc --history --older-than 30d # also the history exports 30 days old or more
 devvm gc --force # delete without asking, as a script must

Options 

 --caches then free devvm's share of Lima's own caches, after asking
 -f, --force don't ask to confirm, which devvm needs without a terminal or with --no-input
 -h, --help help for gc
 --history also delete the saved exports of agents' history
 --nix-cache also delete the whole shared Nix cache
 --older-than DURATION with --history, only those older than DURATION, such as 30d
 --orphans also delete what devvm keeps for VMs their backend no longer has
 --retention then apply the retention settings
 --tool-images also delete the current shared tool images no VM has, or only those of the TOOLs named

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it
 -v, --verbose show the output of the commands devvm runs instead of a status line

Docs

item.title: devvm git-protect

Examples

 devvm git-protect off # unlock .git, once the VM is stopped
 devvm git-protect on # lock .git again as it is then

devvm group join NAME [flags]

Examples 

 devvm group join web # join the group web
 devvm group join web --as api2 # join it as api2 instead of this folder's name

Options

 -h, --help help for join
 --here use this folder's own VM, never that of a folder it's inside
 --parent use the VM of the nearest folder this one is inside, even across a git repo of its own

Options inherited from parent commands 

 --no-input never ask, and fail where devvm would ask, naming the flag that answers it

item.title: devvm group leave
item.description:
Take this folder’s VM out of its group

Synopsis

Take this folder’s VM out of its group, and remove the links the group made, in this VM and in the group’s other VMs, naming them. The links you made with devvm link add stay, and the group goes with its last VM.

devvm group leave [flags]

Examples 

 devvm group leave # leave this folder's VM's group

Options
